question: Which of the following state High Court's jurisdiction extends to the Union Territories of Daman and Diu?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bombay High Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bombay High Court has jurisdiction over the state of Maharashtra and the Union Territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.
 
• It was one of the three High Courts in India established at the Presidency towns by the Letters patent granted by Her Majesty Queen Victoria, bearing date June 26, 1862.
 
• The High Court is located in Mumbai, the capital city of Maharashtra.
 
• The court has regional branches at Nagpur, Aurangabad, and Panaji (Goa).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High Courts in India**

 
 
• India has a high court in each state and union territory, although some high courts have jurisdiction over more than one state or union territory.
 
• High Courts are the principal civil courts of original jurisdiction in each state and union territory, and they are empowered to hear both civil and criminal matters.
 
• They also have the power to hear appeals from lower courts and to issue writs for enforcing fundamental rights.
 
• The judges of the High Courts are appointed by the President of India in consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the governor of the state.
 
 
 
• **Union Territories of Daman and Diu**
 
 
• Daman and Diu were two separate districts of the union territory of Daman and Diu until 2019.
 
• In 2020, they were merged with Dadra and Nagar Haveli to form the new union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.
 
• These territories were part of Portuguese India until they were annexed by India in 1961.
 
• The High Court with jurisdiction over these territories is the Bombay High Court.
 
 
 
• **Jurisdiction**
 
 
• Jurisdiction refers to the official power to make legal decisions and judgments.
 
• In the context of High Courts, it refers to the geographic area or the range of cases over which the court has authority.
 
• Some High Courts have jurisdiction over multiple states or union territories, while others are limited to a single state or union territory.
 
• The jurisdiction of a High Court can be extended or altered by legislation.
